caption:
This morning, I showed why OpenAI’s Decisions API matters: it gives production workflows a typed decision layer instead of just another agent reply.

2.1× measured cost per call vs Jev on one 2,759-call benchmark.
1,469 ms p99 latency vs 526 ms in that same head-to-head test.
Image support is there, but the reference says no external image URLs or file IDs.

My take: production AI is not about sounding smart. It is about measuring cost, tails, and limits before the decision touches the operation.

Comment AGENTES and I will send you the details by DM.

scenes: This morning, we looked at OpenAI putting the Decisions API into public beta for typed decision flows in production. I went back in to check the pricing, the direct benchmark, and one product limit.
First, an independent benchmark measured the Decisions API at 2.1 times the cost per call versus Jev on the same workload.
Second, the same test says median speed was basically tied, but at p99 the Decisions API had a much longer tail.
Third, the API supports images, but the reference says external image URLs and file IDs are not supported right now.
My take: typed decisions are useful, but shipping means checking latency tails, real call cost, and operational limits before wiring it into production.
